$comment: GENERATED by tools/autoresearch.py --render -- do not edit. The source of truth is autoresearch/results.tsv plus autoresearch/runs/*.json. CI regenerates this and fails on any diff, so a number on the site cannot stop matching the run that produced it.

protocol.loss_axis: mean loss over the last 50 of 1000 steps, at seed 42
protocol.speed_axis: steps per second, median of 3 runs of the whole process

thresholds.rule: keep if (loss down at least loss_material and speed no worse than speed_tolerance) or (speed up at least speed_material and loss no worse than loss_tolerance), and the run learned
thresholds.note: loss_material and speed_material are noise floors, tolerances are regression limits; they are different numbers on purpose. The justification for each is in the comment above its definition in tools/autoresearch.py.

objective.decided_by: tools/autoresearch.py, from measured medians. The model proposes an edit and never states a verdict.

model.verification: GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models -> this id is listed, name 'Space Bunny Alpha', context_length 1000000, supported_parameters includes reasoning_effort. A 1-token POST to the chat endpoint with reasoning_effort='max' returned 200; the same request with an unrecognised value returned HTTP 400 'expected one of "max"|"xhigh"|"high"|"medium"|"low"|"minimal"|"none"'. The reasoning object form {effort: ...} also works but cannot be combined with reasoning.max_tokens, so the top-level parameter is the one to use.
model.pricing_note: prompt and completion are both priced at 0 on this model as of the verification date, so a session costs tokens rather than money. The harness still reports total token usage per experiment in the run record, because a free model today is not a promise about tomorrow.

runner.note: The speed axis is only comparable within a session. The baseline is rebuilt from source and re-measured every session for this reason; benchmarks/results.json was taken on a different machine and is not used.

baseline.description: the frozen track, unmodified, as this session's comparator

best.description: Hoist Adam bias corrections and fuse each parameter update into one arena borrow

runs.description: the frozen track, unmodified, as this session's comparator

runs.reason: no axis improved materially: discarded: loss +0.1%, speed -4.8%; failing loss_material, speed_material
runs.description: Make RMSNorm differentiable through its mean square and inverse square root
Collapse each linear layer output into one direct dot-product tape node
Avoid cloning parent and local-gradient vectors during every backward pass
Fuse linear dot products into correctly differentiated tape nodes
Fuse attention score dot products into the existing linear tape node
Reset only graph nodes visited during each backward pass

runs.reason: no axis improved materially: discarded: loss -7.0%, speed +1735.8%; failing learned, loss_material, loss_tolerance
runs.description: Hold Adam at 0.01 for all 1000 steps instead of linearly annealing to zero
Shifted logsumexp cross entropy skips unused vocabulary probabilities
Fuse constant affine operations into single tape nodes with identical arithmetic
Fuse attention value mixtures into one correctly differentiated tape node per output
Fuse shifted exponentials and sums into fewer correctly differentiated tape nodes
Store tape dependencies in one allocation per node without changing arithmetic
Use a flat autograd edge arena and recycle the graph after each step with identical arithmetic
Fuse cross entropy and division and batch Adam arena updates
Fuse attention softmax normalization and cached value mixing into one tape node per head output
Lower Adam beta2 to 0.98 for faster second-moment adaptation
Fuse analytically differentiated RMSNorm into one tape node per output
Differentiate RMSNorm through its mean square and inverse scale on the autograd tape
Hoist Adam bias corrections and fuse each parameter update into one arena borrow
Share each softmax denominator and fuse its probability divisions into one tape node
Fuse RMSNorm scale and cross entropy into analytically differentiated tape nodes
Replace the per-step topological DFS with reverse arena-order backpropagation
Reduce repeated arena borrows in hot tensor primitives with identical arithmetic
Share softmax reciprocals and reuse tape reduction scratch to accelerate training without changing model arithmetic
Double Adam learning rate to 0.02 and restore beta2 to 0.99

caveats: The speed axis is only comparable within one session. It was measured on the machine named under `runner`, and a ratio against a number from another machine is a number about that machine. `benchmarks/results.json` is not used as the baseline for exactly this reason.

The loss axis is deterministic at a fixed seed: the track's PRNG is xoshiro256++ with SplitMix64 seeding, so a given candidate produces a given loss curve or it does not. The speed axis is not, and is the median of 3 runs.

Wall clock here is the whole process, including startup and the twenty-sample inference pass. Both are small and both are constant, and the baseline is measured the same way in the same session, so the comparison is fair. The absolute figure is not a pure training time.

A loss number cannot tell a correct gradient from a wrong one -- the C port's is wrong by a factor of -8 and its loss curve still tracks the reference to within 7% (docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md issue 1). Every candidate is finite-difference checked before it competes; see `grad_ratio` on each row.
